topic: The Central Limit Theorem (CLT): From Chaos to Order

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of Distributions
lecture_lines: Other distributions appear skewed or uniform.
animations: 5. Side-by-side comparison of Uniform vs. Skewed distributions.

sections.title: The Problem: Does the Parent Distribution Matter?
lecture_lines: Does the parent distribution shape matter?
Do sample means follow original patterns?
animations: 1. Display 'Parent Population' histogram with irregular data points.
2. 'Professor Squirrel' icon appears and picks 5 random samples.

sections.title: The Experiment: Building the Sampling Distribution
lecture_lines: Take many samples of size n.
Calculate the mean for each sample.
Plot means as size n increases.
Observe the shape transforming into curves.
Bell shapes emerge from chaotic data.
animations: 2. Rapid accumulation of sample means in new histogram.
3. Final histogram animation showing emergence of bell-curve shape (Gold: #f1c40f).

sections.title: The Core Revelation: The Central Limit Theorem
lecture_lines: The Central Limit Theorem defines this.
Sample means approach a Normal Distribution.
Valid for any original population shape.
Required sample size typically n equals 30.
Chaos transforms into stable bell curves.
animations: 1. Display formula for CLT, clearly showing 'Normal Distribution' transition.
2. 'Chaotic Cloud' transformation: fade points to form smooth Bell Curve.
5. Final full Bell Curve with standard deviation shaded area (Purple: #9b59b6).

sections.title: Why It Matters: Real-World Application
lecture_lines: CLT is the foundation of inference.
We predict populations from small samples.
Accurate estimates require minimal data points.
animations: 1. Display 'Smartphone App' icon scanning battery data points.
2. Show sample mean and standard error confidence bar.
3. Final visual: 'Population Inference' text linking sample to reality.
